newsitem.title: USA: Healthdyne stock up as Georgia nixes bill.
newsitem.headline: Healthdyne stock up as Georgia nixes bill.

text.p: Shares of Healthdyne Technologies Inc rose sharply on views Invacare Corp will aggressively pursue its $166 million hostile takeover of the medical device firm following the rejection of a Georgia measure that could have crushed its effort.
The stock of Marietta, Ga.-based Healthdyne gained $1.875 to $13.50 -- about where it had been trading before the legislative action earlier this month sent the shares tumbling to about $11.
"The fight is not over, but it has been made less difficult," said one trader of takeover stocks.

Healthdyne has rejected Invacare's $13 per share offer, saying that the company is not for sale. Wall Street sources have speculated that the company might consider an offer in the $18-per-share range.

Invacare's hostile effort was dealt a near-fatal blow last week when the Georgia state senate approved a measure to require public companies to stagger the election of board diretors. The measure would have severely curtailed any hostile takeover attempts in which an unwelcome bidder sought to take control by replacing a company's board.

But the measure itself was dealt a setback on Tuesday when the state's house of representatives voted against it and sent it back to the Senate. The measure was expected to reach a House-Senate conference committee on Thursday.

Wall Street sources expect Invacare, which had blasted the Georgia legislative effort, to now pursue its takeover by nominating candidates to replace Healthdyne's board at the company's yet-unscheduled annual shareholders meeting.
The latest Georgia action "certainly gives Invacare an incentive to hang in there," said Steven Cohen, head of research at New York arbitrage firm Kellner, DiLeo & Co.
Wall Street sources said Healthdyne shares may edge up to more than $14 in the near-term as Invacare moves ahead with its effort.
Shares of Invacare gained $0.75 to $24 per share in late morning trade.
